<untrusted_issue number="18" title="Some links in our chat logs are not clickable">
We render our team chat logs to HTML with mistune (`plugins=["url"]`) and people keep complaining that "some links are dead text".

For example this log line:

```
alice: docs are at www.example.com/docs, or the old page https://example.com/old
```

The second link is clickable, the first one isn't, even though it is clearly an address. Our users paste addresses all kinds of ways and expect them to work like on GitHub or in Slack.

Could the url plugin be smarter about this? Not sure what the right rules are, but we'd like the obvious ones to just work without breaking the links that already work.

</untrusted_issue>

# Software Requirements Specification: URL Plugin Enhancements for WWW Links - **Document ID:** SRS-issue-18 - **Version:** v1 - **Date:** 2026-11-24 - **Status:** DRAFT - **Verdict:** PARTIALLY-READY - **Companion files:** REG-issue-18-v1.md, VAL-issue-18-v1.md - **Interaction mode:** batch (headless execution, no stakeholder available) > **Legend.** *Origin:* STATED = said in a source · CONFIRMED = inference confirmed by a stakeholder · > INFERRED = the analyst's inference (see linked ASM). *Readiness:* READY · NEEDS-CONFIRMATION · > NEEDS-CLARIFICATION · BLOCKED. INFERRED items are never READY. ## 1. Introduction ### 1.1 Purpose This document specifies requirements for enhancing the `url` plugin in the Python Markdown library `mistune` to recognize scheme-less URLs starting with `www.`, enabling team chat logs and user-pasted text containing `www.example.com` links to render as clickable HTML links without breaking existing functionality. ### 1.2 Problem statement (as given) We render our team chat logs to HTML with mistune (`plugins=["url"]`) and people keep complaining that "some links are dead text". For example this log line: `alice: docs are at www.example.com/docs, or the old page https://example.com/old`. The second link is clickable, the first one isn't, even though it is clearly an address. Our users paste addresses all kinds of ways and expect them to work like on GitHub or in Slack. Could the url plugin be smarter about this? Not sure what the right rules are, but we'd like the obvious ones to just work without breaking the links that already work. ### 1.3 Scope - **In scope (stated):** Recognizing raw URLs starting with `www.` in addition to existing `http://` and `https://` URLs, without breaking existing links (SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-003, SRC-004, SRC-005). - **In scope (inferred, pending confirmation):** Prepending `https://` to scheme-less `www.` URLs in generated `href` attributes (ASM-001); pattern boundary rules for `www.` links (ASM-002). - **Out of scope:** Automatic linking of arbitrary domain names without `www.` prefix (e.g. `example.com/docs`) (OOS-001). ### 1.4 Success measures Obvious raw `www.` URLs (e.g. `www.example.com/docs`) render as clickable HTML links `www.example.com/docs`, while existing valid links and non-link text remain unaffected. ## 2. Functional requirements ### FR-001 — Recognition of scheme-less `www.` URLs - **Statement:** The URL plugin shall recognize and parse raw text matching `www.` URL patterns as link tokens when the url plugin is enabled. - **Actor/Trigger:** ACT-001 - **Origin:** INFERRED - **Sources:** SRC-003, SRC-005 - **Assumptions:** ASM-002 - **Priority:** Must (stated) - **Readiness:** NEEDS-CONFIRMATION - **Blocked by:** None - **Open questions:** OQ-002 - **Evidence:** None - **Verification:** Test - **Acceptance criteria:** - AC-FR-001-1: Given Markdown input `"visit www.example.com/docs"` with url plugin enabled, when `mistune.html(markdown, plugins=['url'])` is called, then exact observable output is `"

# Assumptions and Open-Questions Register: URL Plugin Enhancements for WWW Links

- **Document ID:** REG-issue-18
- **Version:** v1
- **Date:** 2026-11-24

## 1. Open questions

### OQ-001 — Scheme selection for `www.` URLs in href attribute
- **Question:** Should `www.example.com` links have `https://` prepended to their HTML `href` attribute, or `http://`, or should the scheme be configurable?
- **Why it matters:** Browsers require an absolute URI scheme (like `https://`) in `href` to navigate correctly when clicking relative/scheme-less domains.
- **Options:** (a) Always prepend `https://` (b) Always prepend `http://` (c) Make protocol configurable via plugin options
- **Default if unanswered:** ASM-001 (always prepend `https://`)
- **Owner:** STK-001 / maintainers
- **Blocking:** no
- **Affects:** FR-003
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Answer:** —

### OQ-002 — Exact regular expression boundary rules for `www.` matching
- **Question:** What exact regular expression boundaries should distinguish valid `www.` URLs from partial word matches (e.g. `my_www.example.com`)?
- **Why it matters:** Overly broad regex could break code blocks or ordinary words containing `www.`.
- **Options:** (a) Require whitespace, angle bracket, or start of line before `www.` (b) Require word boundary (`\b`) before `www.`
- **Default if unanswered:** ASM-002 (require word boundary / non-word character before `www.`)
- **Owner:** STK-001 / maintainers
- **Blocking:** no
- **Affects:** FR-001, FR-004
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Answer:** —

## 2. Assumptions

### ASM-001 — Default scheme for `www.` href
- **Statement:** Scheme-less URLs starting with `www.` should automatically prepend `https://` to their `href` attribute in generated HTML links.
- **Basis:** Modern web standards and security best practices default to HTTPS for web navigation.
- **Origin:** INFERRED
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Confirm via:** OQ-001
- **Affects:** FR-003

### ASM-002 — Boundary pattern for `www.` matching
- **Statement:** The matching pattern for `www.` URLs should ensure that `www.` is preceded by a word boundary or whitespace/start-of-line to avoid matching inside identifiers or words.
- **Basis:** Standard text parsing conventions for autolinks in markdown libraries (GitHub Flavored Markdown / Slack behavior).
- **Origin:** INFERRED
- **Status:** OPEN
- **Confirm via:** OQ-002
- **Affects:** FR-001, FR-004

## 3. Conflicts

### CNF-001 — None identified
- **Claim A:** —
- **Claim B:** —
- **Nature:** source vs source
- **Affects:** —
- **Resolution options:** —
- **Decision owner:** —

## 4. Out of scope

### OOS-001 — Arbitrary domain autolinking without `www.`
- **Item:** Automatic linking of arbitrary domain names lacking both protocol scheme and `www.` prefix (e.g., `example.com/docs`).
- **Basis:** Not requested by issue #18 ("obvious ones to just work", specifying `www.example.com/docs`).
